requirement:
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate one evidence detail
page for every requirement and named example defined in a rendered chapter.
Each page MUST be a subchapter of the index chapter, in definition order,
titled by the definition's full name, at a path derived from the index chapter's
path.
Books configured by {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` fold these subchapters in the
sidebar until a reader expands the index chapter.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.index.detail_pages`. Each obligation maps to a marked test, as follows.

**One page per requirement and named example.**
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` defines two requirements, one example and a nested child chapter's requirement. It asserts that the index has exactly four detail pages besides the coverage page, so a page exists for the example too.
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` covers requirements in every evidence state: recorded true, recorded false, changed, absent and uncovered. It checks that a page is generated for each, including `requirements.core.absent`, which has no evidence file.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons]` includes an example definition.
- `tests/outcomes.rs#fn[valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book]` and `tests/repository.rs#fn[mdbook_preprocessor_renders_definitions_between_stdin_and_stdout]` cover pages through the CLI and preprocessor path.

**Subchapters of the index chapter, in definition order.**
- The default-index test asserts the exact name sequence `["rules.zeta","rules.alpha","rules.cli.mdbook","rules.child.nested"]`. That sequence mixes requirements and an example, and it crosses chapters, including a nested child chapter.
- It also asserts `parent_names == ["Requirements index"]` and section numbers `[3, offset+2]` for each page.
- The explicit-index test asserts the order `Documented coverage gaps`, `Existing`, `rules.zeta`, `more.cli.mdbook`. The pre-existing child stays ahead of the generated pages. It also asserts `parent_names` of `["Index"]` and number `[3,4]` for the last page.
- The repository test asserts the same order through the binary.

**Titled by full name.** The tests assert `chapter.name` equals `requirements.core.ready`, `rules.zeta`, `more.cli.mdbook` and so on. The namespace is derived from the chapter path, and a name with a dot is kept as a dot in the title.

**Path derived from the index chapter's path.**
- With the index at `appendix/requirements-index.md`, the page path is `appendix/requirements-index/requirements.core.ready.md`.
- With the generated index at `requirements-index.md`, the default-index test checks the coverage page path `requirements-index/coverage.md`, and the links in the pages (`href="requirements-index/rules.cli%2Emdbook.html"`, `../requirements-index/rules.child.nested.html`) point at the derived directory.
- The explicit-index test uses `appendix/index.md` and checks `appendix/index/more.cli%2Emdbook.html`.
- These cover root and nested index locations and an escaped dot in the name.

**Sidebar folding for books configured by `requirements.cli.setup`.** This is a cited requirement, so I only checked that its application is tested. `tests/setup.rs#fn[setup_is_repeatable]` asserts that `output.html.fold.enable` is set to true, and appears once. `tests/setup.rs#fn[setup_keeps_an_existing_fold_setting]` checks that an existing fold setting is kept. Folding itself is mdBook behaviour. The generated subchapters being sub-items of the index chapter is asserted in the tests above.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behaviour that the tests would accept. A missing page, wrong order, wrong title, wrong parent or wrong path would each fail an exact assertion. The implementation (`src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]`) skips chapters that have no path, which is a reasonable reading of "rendered chapter" and is not something the requirement text distinguishes further.

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, enable sidebar folding with `output.html.fold.enable` unless the book already sets it, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and MUST NOT overwrite a differing test or stylesheet. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.
